meta.title: Synthetic fixture — offline collaboration research atlas
meta.updated: fixture day 4 (not an actual research date)
meta.goal: Synthetic teaching example: explore offline-first collaborative editing mechanisms for maintainers of shared workspace software. No real research, sources, experiments, or audience endorsement are represented.
meta.standing: All rounds, scores, source labels, and reviewer roles are simulated. No actual independent evaluation occurred; no proposal passes. Four areas retain three unsearched routes and two active investigations.
meta.standard: Illustrative gates: novelty 94 / audience impact 94. Novelty = min(research novelty, idea novelty). Best means highest novelty + audience impact among scored rounds, display only, not a third gate. Changed rubrics/audiences/constraints make rounds noncomparable; none changes in this synthetic fixture. Potential is not measured success. Sources are fictional no-link labels.
meta.what_worked: Within the synthetic scenario, separating merge correctness, permission authority, recovery cost, and user agency exposed genuinely different next questions.

risks.title: Synthetic sources are not evidence
risks.text: SIM-S1–SIM-S8 are invented no-link labels, not real citations or claims about existing software.
risks.check: Replace the entire scenario with actual located primary sources and receipts before using it for a real decision.

risks.title: Constraints can disappear in a pivot
risks.text: Weakening offline revocation to expiry changes the guarantee; a useful fallback cannot silently become the original promise.
risks.check: Keep the original constraint visible and obtain any required user authorization before changing it.

risks.title: A best score is not a pass
risks.text: R7's simulated 92/93 is below both 94 gates, and its repair premise is unresolved.
risks.check: Use the actual current review, constraints, and independence evidence; never promote an atlas summary into approval.

results.text: Best synthetic result remains 92/93; now isolate cascading dependencies rather than resubmit unchanged text.

lessons.pattern: Domain changes can hide identical machinery.
lessons.evidence: Synthetic R1/SIM-S1 and R5/SIM-S5 close two repackaged mechanisms.
lessons.check: State the guarantee remaining after the strongest baseline, with a distinguishing trace.

lessons.pattern: Partition claims need an information premise.
lessons.evidence: Synthetic R3/SIM-S3 defeats instantaneous revocation without a new local observation.
lessons.check: Write two indistinguishable local histories before claiming a remote event is known.

lessons.pattern: Explanation polish is not yet an explanation contribution.
lessons.evidence: Synthetic R6 is 90/87; SIM-S6 already previews operations. R9 relabels SIM-S8.
lessons.check: Specify the user's decision and a different observable guarantee, not renamed controls.

lessons.pattern: Component novelty cannot hide a familiar overall idea.
lessons.evidence: Synthetic R7: research novelty 95, idea novelty 92, so novelty is 92.
lessons.check: Assess both dimensions and take their minimum; test the dependency-summary premise.
